study type: Secondary analysis of cross-sectional survey data
cohort: The study included 2,256 survey respondents from PRAMS who answered a question about taking childbirth classes during their most recent pregnancy.
finding: Attending childbirth education was associated with reduced likelihood of primary cesarean, increased attendance at postpartum visits, increased use of birth control, safer infant sleep practices, and increased breastfeeding, though benefits varied across demographic groups.
mod_finding: Childbirth education was associated with a reduced likelihood of primary cesarean.
cross-section timing: Postpartum period (data collected via PRAMS survey)
